AEROM_ALT_ABORT.d: Maximum allowable loss in altitude during a trick or sequence from its starting altitude.

AEROM_ANG_TC.d: This is the time over which we filter the desired roll to smooth it

AEROM_DEBUG.d: This controls the printing of extra debug information on paths

AEROM_ENTRY_RATE.d: This controls how rapidly we roll into a new orientation

AEROM_ERR_COR_D.d: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

AEROM_ERR_COR_P.d: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path

AEROM_KE_RUDD.d: Percent of rudder normally uses to sustain knife-edge at trick speed

AEROM_KE_RUDD_LK.d: Time to look ahead in the path to calculate rudder correction for bank angle

AEROM_LKAHD.d: This is how much time to look ahead in the path for calculating path rates

AEROM_MIS_ANGLE.d: When set to a non-zero value, this is the assumed direction of the mission. Otherwise the waypoint angle is used

AEROM_PATH_SCALE.d: Scale factor for Path/Box size. 0.5 would half the distances in maneuvers. Radii are unaffected.

AEROM_ROL_COR_TC.d: This is the time constant for correcting roll errors. A smaller value leads to faster roll corrections

AEROM_SPD_I.d: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

AEROM_SPD_P.d: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error

AEROM_STALL_PIT.d: Pitch threashold for moving to final stage of stall turn

AEROM_STALL_THR.d: Amount of throttle to reduce to for a stall turn

AEROM_THR_BOOST.d: This is the extra throttle added in schedule elements marked as needing a throttle boost

AEROM_THR_LKAHD.d: This controls how far ahead we look in time along the path for the target throttle

AEROM_THR_PIT_FF.d: This controls how much extra throttle to add based on pitch ange. The value is for 90 degrees and is applied in proportion to pitch

AEROM_TIME_COR_P.d: This is the time constant for correcting path position errors

AEROM_TS_I.d: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

AEROM_TS_P.d: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync

AEROM_TS_RATE.d: This sets the rate we send data for time sync between aircraft

AEROM_TS_SPDMAX.d: This sets the maximum speed adjustment for time sync between aircraft

AEROM_YAW_ACCEL.d: This is maximum yaw acceleration to use

AHRS_ORIG_ALT.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this altitude (in meters above sea level) if not already set

AHRS_ORIG_LAT.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this latitude if not already set

AHRS_ORIG_LON.d: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this longitude if not already set

ALAND_WP_ALT.d: Altitude of final approach waypoint created by script

ALAND_WP_DIST.d: Distance from landing point (HOME) to final approach waypoint created by script in the opposite direction of initial takeoff

ARM_C_RTL_ALT_M.d: RTL_ALT_M should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_ESTOP.d: Emergency Stop disables arming. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_FENCE.d: Fences loaded but no fence enabled. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_FOLL_OFS_DEF.d: Follow offsets should not be left as default (zero) if FOLL_ENABLE = 1. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_FOLL_SYSID.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID has been set. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_FOLL_SYSID_X.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID is different to MAV_SYSID. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_MNTX_SYSID.d: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1 and MNTx_SYSID_DEFLT is set, check that FOLL_SYSID is equal MNTx. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_AIRSPEED.d: Validate that AIRSPEED_STALL(if set) < MIN < CRUISE < MAX d. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_QRTL_ALT.d: Q_RTL_ALT should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_Q_FS_LAND.d: Notify the user that on failsafe a QuadPlan will land. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_Q_FS_RTL.d: Notify the user that on failsafe a QuadPlan will QRTL. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_RTL_ALT.d: RTL_ALTITITUDE should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_SCALING.d: Validate that SCALING_SPEED is within 20% of AIRSPEED_CRUISE. If SCALING_SPEED changes the vehicle may need to be retuned. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_P_STALL.d: Validate that AIRSPEED_MIN is at least 25% above AIRSPEED_STALL(if set). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_RALLY.d: Rally Point more than RALLY_LIMIT_KM kilometers away. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_RTL_CLIMB.d: RTL_CLIMB_MIN should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_SYSID.d: Check that MAV_SYSID (or SYDID_THISMAV) has been set. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable. -1=Disabled, 0=Emergency(PreArm), 1=Alert(PreArm), 2=Critical(PreArm), 3=Error(PreArm), 4=Warning, 5=Notice, 6=Info, 7=Debug.

ARM_V_ALT_LEGAL.d: Legal max altitude for UAV/RPAS/drones in your jurisdiction

BATT_IDX.d: Ensure this battery is configured with `BATT*_MONITOR=29`.

BTAG_CUR_CYCLES.d: this is the highest value for battery cycles for all connected batteries

CAM1_THERM_GAIN.d: thermal image temperature range. -1=Leave Unchanged, 0=LowGain (50C to 550C), 1=HighGain (-20C to 150C).

CAM1_THERM_RAW.d: save images with raw temperatures. -1=Leave Unchanged, 0=Disabled (30fps), 1=Enabled (25 fps).

CFACT.d: This is multiplicative factor to correct the measured flow. Set to <1 if your sensor measures too high.

CGA_RATIO.d: The ratio between the front and back motor outputs during steady-state hover. Positive when the CoG is in front of the motors midpoint (front motors work harder).

DCS1_BATT_IDX.d: Battery monitor instance to feed with this circuit. Set to 1 for BATT, 2 for BATT2 etc. The corresponding BATTn_MONITOR must be 29 (scripting). Set to 0 to disable.

DCS1_CIRCUIT_ID.d: circuit_id of the CircuitStatus message to use for this instance. Set to -1 to disable.

DCS_NUM_CIRCUITS.d: Number of DroneCAN CircuitStatus battery monitor instances. The per-instance DCSx_ parameters are created based on this value.

DIST_CUTOFF.d: The distance from target beyond which the target is ignored

DJIR_DEBUG.d: Enable DJIRS2 debug. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Enabled with attitude reporting.

DJIR_UPSIDEDOWN.d: DJIRS2 upside down. 0=Right side up, 1=Upside down.

DR_ENABLE_DIST.d: Distance from home (in meters) beyond which the dead reckoning will be enabled

DR_FLY_ALT_MIN.d: Copter will fly at at least this altitude (in meters) above home during deadreckoning

DR_FLY_TIMEOUT.d: Copter will attempt to switch to NEXT_MODE after this many seconds of deadreckoning. If it cannot switch modes it will continue in Guided_NoGPS. Set to 0 to disable timeout

DR_GPS_SACC_MAX.d: GPS speed accuracy maximum, above which deadreckoning home will begin (default is 0.8). Lower values trigger with good GPS quality, higher values will allow poorer GPS before triggering. Set to 0 to disable use of GPS speed accuracy

DR_GPS_SAT_MIN.d: GPS satellite count threshold below which deadreckoning home will begin (default is 6). Higher values trigger with good GPS quality, Lower values trigger with worse GPS quality. Set to 0 to disable use of GPS satellite count

DR_GPS_TRIGG_SEC.d: GPS checks must fail for this many seconds before dead reckoning will be triggered

DR_NEXT_MODE.d: Copter switch to this mode after GPS recovers or DR_FLY_TIMEOUT has elapsed. Default is 6/RTL. Set to -1 to return to mode used before deadreckoning was triggered. 16=PosHold, 17=Brake, 2=AltHold, 20=Guided_NoGPS, 21=Smart_RTL, 27=Auto RTL, 3=Auto, 4=Guided, 5=Loiter, 6=RTL, 7=Circle, 9=Land.

EFI_2K_CANDRV.d: NMEA 2000 CAN driver. Use 1 for first CAN scripting driver, 2 for 2nd driver. 0=Disabled, 1=FirstCAN, 2=SecondCAN.

EFI_DLA_LPS.d: EFI DLA litres of fuel per second of injection time

EFI_H6K_CANDRV.d: Halo6000 CAN driver. Use 1 for first CAN scripting driver, 2 for 2nd driver. 0=Disabled, 1=FirstCAN, 2=SecondCAN.

EFI_H6K_FUELTOT.d: The capacity of the tank in litres

EFI_H6K_START_FN.d: The RC auxilliary function number for start/stop of the generator. Zero to disable start function. 0=Disabled, 300=300, 301=301, 302=302, 303=303, 304=304, 305=305, 306=306, 307=307.

EFI_H6K_TELEM_RT.d: The rate that additional generator telemetry is sent

EFI_HFE_ECU_IDX.d: HFI EFI ECU index, 0 for automatic

EFI_HFE_FUEL_DTY.d: HFI EFI fuel density in gram per litre

EFI_INF_IGN_AUX.d: EFI INF throttle ignition aux function

EFI_SP_GEN_FN.d: SkyPower EFI generator control function. This is the RCn_OPTION value to use to find the R/C channel used for controlling generator start/stop. 0=Disabled, 300=300, 301=301, 302=302, 303=303, 304=304, 305=305, 306=306, 307=307.

EFI_SP_LOG_RT.d: SkyPower EFI log rate. This is the rate at which extra logging of the SkyPower EFI is performed

EFI_SP_MIN_RPM.d: SkyPower EFI minimum RPM. This is the RPM below which the engine is considered to be stopped

EFI_SP_RST_TIME.d: SkyPower EFI restart time. If engine should be running and it has stopped for this amount of time then auto-restart. To disable this feature set this value to zero.

EFI_SP_START_FN.d: SkyPower EFI start function. This is the RCn_OPTION value to use to find the R/C channel used for controlling engine start. 0=Disabled, 300=300, 301=301, 302=302, 303=303, 304=304, 305=305, 306=306, 307=307.

EFI_SP_ST_DISARM.d: SkyPower EFI allow start disarmed. This controls if starting the engine while disarmed is allowed. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

EFI_SP_THR_FN.d: SkyPower EFI throttle function. This sets which SERVOn_FUNCTION to use for the target throttle. This should be 70 for fixed wing aircraft and 31 for helicopter rotor speed control. 0=Disabled, 31=HeliRSC, 70=FixedWing.

EFI_SP_THR_RATE.d: SkyPower EFI throttle rate. This sets rate at which throttle updates are sent to the engine

EFI_SP_TLM_RT.d: SkyPower EFI telemetry rate. This is the rate at which extra telemetry values are sent to the GCS

EFI_SVF_ARMCHECK.d: Check for Generator ARM state before arming. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

ENABLE.d: When set to 0 this script will not run. When set to 1 this script will run.

ESC_HW_OFS.d: Motor number offset of first ESC

ESC_HW_POLES.d: Number of motor poles for eRPM scaling

ESRC_EXTN_QUAL.d: ExternalNav may be used if quality is above this threshold

ESRC_EXTN_THRESH.d: ExternalNav may be used if innovations are below this threshold

ESRC_FLOW_QUAL.d: OpticalFlow may be used if quality is above this threshold

ESRC_FLOW_THRESH.d: OpticalFlow may be used if innovations are below this threshold

ESRC_RNGFND_MAX.d: OpticalFlow may be used if rangefinder distance is below this threshold

FLTMODE_GCSBLOCK.d: Bitmask of flight modes to disable for GCS selection. Mode can still be accessed via RC or failsafe.

FOLLP_ACT_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for Plane Follow enable/disable

FOLLP_ALT.d: When non zero, this altitude value (in FOLL_ALT_TYPE frame) overrides the value sent by the target vehicle

FOLLP_DIST_CLOSE.d: When closer than this distance assume we track by heading

FOLLP_D_D.d: D gain for the speed PID controller distance component

FOLLP_D_I.d: I gain for the speed PID distance component

FOLLP_D_P.d: P gain for the speed PID controller distance component

FOLLP_EXIT_MODE.d: Mode to switch to when follow mode is exited normally

FOLLP_FAIL_MODE.d: Mode to switch to if the target is lost (no signal or > FOLL_DIST_MAX).

FOLLP_LkAHD.d: Time to "lookahead" when calculating distance errors

FOLLP_OVRSHT_DEG.d: If the target is greater than this many degrees left or right, assume an overshoot

FOLLP_REFRESH.d: refresh rate for Plane Follow updates

FOLLP_SIM_TLF_FN.d: Set this switch to simulate losing telemetry from the other vehicle

FOLLP_TIMEOUT.d: How long to try reaquire a target if telemetry from the lead vehicle is lost.

FOLLP_TURN_DEG.d: If the target is greater than this many degrees left or right, assume it's turning

FOLLP_V_D.d: D gain for the speed PID controller velocity component

FOLLP_V_I.d: I gain for the speed PID controller velocity component

FOLLP_V_P.d: P gain for the speed PID controller velocity component

FOLLP_WIDE_TURNS.d: Use wide turns when following a turning target. Alternative is "cutting the corner"

FOLLP_XT_D.d: D term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller

FOLLP_XT_I.d: I term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller

FOLLP_XT_I_MAX.d: maximum I applied the crosstrack/heading PID controller

FOLLP_XT_MAX.d: maximum correction retured by the crosstrack/heading PID controller

FOLLP_XT_P.d: P term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller

FOLT_MAV_CHAN.d: MAVLink channel to which FOLLOW_TARGET should be sent

LTE_BAND.d: This allows selection of LTE band. A value of -1 means no band setting change is made. A value of 0 sets all bands. Otherwise the specified band is set.

LTE_BAUD.d: Baud rate for the serial port to the LTE modem when connected. Initial power on baudrate is in LTE_IBAUD. 115200=115200, 19200=19200, 230400=230400, 3686400=3686400, 38400=38400, 460800=460800, 57600=57600, 921600=921600.

LTE_ENABLE.d: Enable or disable the LTE modem driver. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

LTE_IBAUD.d: This is the initial baud rate on power on for the modem. This is set in the modem with the AT+IREX=baud command. 115200=115200, 19200=19200, 230400=230400, 3686400=3686400, 38400=38400, 460800=460800, 57600=57600, 921600=921600.

LTE_MCCMNC.d: This allows selection of network operator. -1=NoChange, 0=Default, 50501=AU-Telstra, 50502=AU-Optus, 50503=AU-Vodafone.

LTE_OPTIONS.d: Options to control the LTE modem driver. If VerboseSignalInfoGCS is set then additional NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT values are sent with verbose signal information

LTE_PROTOCOL.d: The protocol that we will use in communication with the LTE modem. If this is PPP then the LTE_SERVER parameters are not used and instead a PPP connection will be established and you should use the NET_ parameters to enable network ports. If this is MAVLink2 then the LTE_SERVER parameters are used to create a TCP or UDP connection to a single server. 2=MavLink2, 48=PPP.

LTE_SCRPORT.d: Scripting Serial port to use for the LTE modem. This is the index of the SCR_SDEV ports that are set to 2 for "MAVLink2"

LTE_SERPORT.d: Serial port to use for the LTE modem. This is the index of the SERIALn_ ports that are set to 28 for "scripting"

LTE_SERVER_IP0.d: First octet of the server IP address to connect to

LTE_SERVER_IP1.d: Second octet of the server IP address to connect to

LTE_SERVER_IP2.d: Third octet of the server IP address to connect to

LTE_SERVER_IP3.d: Fourth octet of the server IP address to connect to

LTE_SERVER_PORT.d: IPv4 Port of the server to connect to

LTE_TIMEOUT.d: Timeout in seconds for the LTE connection. If no data is received for this time, the connection will be reset. A value of zero disables the timeout

LTE_TX_RATE.d: Maximum data transmit rate to the modem in bytes/second. Use zero for unlimited

MODE.d: 0: The sensor will save the fuel consumption across power resets. 1: The sensor will reset the power consumption.

PLND_ALT_CUTOFF.d: The altitude (rangefinder distance) below which we stop using the precision landing sensor and continue landing

POI_DIST_MAX.d: POI's max distance (in meters) from the vehicle

PORT.d: Which Scripting serial port the sensor is connected at.

PREV_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to used to trigger parameter reversion

QUIK_ANGLE_MAX.d: If while tuning the angle error goes over this limit then the tune will aborts to prevent a bad oscillation in the case of the tuning algorithm failing. If you get an error "Tuning: attitude error ABORTING" and you think it is a false positive then you can either raise this parameter or you can try increasing the QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME to do the tune more slowly. A value of zero disables this check.

QUIK_AUTO_FILTER.d: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

QUIK_AUTO_SAVE.d: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME.d: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.

QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN.d: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune

QUIK_MAX_REDUCE.d: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.

QUIK_OPTIONS.d: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.

QUIK_OSC_SMAX.d: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.

QUIK_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO.d: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain

QUIK_YAW_D_MAX.d: Maximum value for yaw D gain

QUIK_YAW_P_MAX.d: Maximum value for yaw P gain

QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO.d: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain

RCK_DEBUG.d: Sends Rockblock debug text to GCS via statustexts. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

RCK_ENABLE.d: Enables the Rockblock sending and recieving. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

RCK_FORCEHL.d: Automatically enables High Latency mode if not already enabled. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Enabled on telemetry loss.

RCK_PERIOD.d: When in High Latency mode, send Rockblock updates every N seconds

RCK_TIMEOUT.d: If RCK_FORCEHL=2, this is the number of seconds of GCS timeout until High Latency mode is auto-enabled

RK9_BOOTED.d: SERVOn GPIO channel that reads the Rockblock booted state. This connects to I_BTD on the Rockblock header. Requires SERVON_FUNCTION=-1

RK9_DEBUG.d: Sends Rockblock debug text to GCS via statustexts. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

RK9_ENABLE.d: Enables the Rockblock sending and recieving. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

RK9_FORCEHL.d: Automatically enables High Latency mode if not already enabled. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Enabled on telemetry loss.

RK9_PERIOD.d: When in High Latency mode, send Rockblock updates every N seconds

RK9_RELAY.d: RELAYn output to control Rockblock power. This connects to I_EN on the Rockblock header.

RK9_SCRPORT.d: Scripting Serial port number to which the Rockblock is connected for HL2 messages This is the index of the SCR_SDEV ports that are set to 2 for "MavlinkHL"

RK9_SERPORT.d: Serial port number to which the Rockblock is connected.This is the index of the SERIALn_ ports that are set to 28 for "scripting"

RK9_TIMEOUT.d: If RK9_FORCEHL=2, this is the number of seconds of GCS timeout until High Latency mode is auto-enabled

RTUN_AUTO_FILTER.d: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

RTUN_AUTO_SAVE.d: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

RTUN_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

RTUN_SPD_FFRATIO.d: Ratio between measured response and CRUISE_THROTTLE value. Raise this to get a higher CRUISE_THROTTLE value

RTUN_SPD_I_RATIO.d: Ratio between speed FF and I gain. Raise this to get a higher I gain, 0 to leave I unchanged

RTUN_SPD_P_RATIO.d: Ratio between speed FF and P gain. Raise this to get a higher P gain, 0 to leave P unchanged

RTUN_SPEED_MIN.d: The mimimum speed in m/s required for tuning to start

RTUN_STR_FFRATIO.d: Ratio between measured response and FF gain. Raise this to get a higher FF gain

RTUN_STR_I_RATIO.d: Ratio between steering FF and I gains. Raise this to get a higher I gain, 0 to leave I unchanged

RTUN_STR_P_RATIO.d: Ratio between steering FF and P gains. Raise this to get a higher P gain, 0 to leave P unchanged

SHIP_AUTO_OFS.d: Settings this parameter to one triggers an automatic follow offset calculation based on current position of the vehicle and the landing target. NOTE: This parameter will auto-reset to zero once the offset has been calculated. 0=Disabled, 1=Trigger.

SHIP_LAND_ANGLE.d: Angle from the stern of the ship for landing approach. Use this to ensure that on a go-around that ship superstructure and cables are avoided. A value of zero means to approach from the rear of the ship. A value of 90 means the landing will approach from the port (left) side of the ship. A value of -90 will mean approaching from the starboard (right) side of the ship. A value of 180 will approach from the bow of the ship. This parameter is combined with the sign of the RTL_RADIUS parameter to determine the holdoff pattern. If RTL_RADIUS is positive then a clockwise loiter is performed, if RTL_RADIUS is negative then a counter-clockwise loiter is used.

SLUP_DEBUG.d: Slung payload debug output, set to 1 to enable debug. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

SLUP_DIST_MAX.d: Oscillation is suppressed when vehicle and payload are no more than this distance horizontally. Set to 0 to always suppress

SLUP_RESTOFS_TC.d: payload's position estimator's time constant used to compensate for GPS errors and wind. Higher values result in smoother estimate but slower response

SLUP_SYSID.d: Slung Payload mavlink system id. 0 to use any/all system ids

SLUP_VEL_P.d: Slung Payload Velocity P gain, higher values will result in faster movements in sync with payload

SLUP_WP_POS_P.d: WP position P gain. higher values will result in vehicle moving more quickly back to the original waypoint

TA_ACT_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for Terrain Avoidance enable/disable

TA_ALT_MAX.d: This is a limit on how high the terrain avoidane will take the vehicle. It acts a failsafe to prevent vertical flyaways.

TA_CMTC_ENABLE.d: Whether to enable Can't Make That Climb while running Terrain Avoidance

TA_CMTC_HGT.d: The minimum Height above terrain to maintain when following an AUTO mission or RTL. If zero(0) use TA_PTCH_DOW_MIN.

TA_CMTC_RAD.d: Use this radius for the loiter when trying to gain altitude. If not set or <=0 use WP_LOITER_RAD

TA_GSP_AIRBRAKE.d: This is the limit for triggering airbrake to slow groundspeed as a difference between the airspeed and groundspeed. -1 for disabled.

TA_GSP_MAX.d: This is a limit on how fast in groundspeeed terrain avoidance will take the vehicle. This is to allow for reliable sensor readings. -1 for disabled.

TA_HOME_DIST.d: Terrain avoidance will not be applied if the vehicle is less than this distance from home

TA_PTCH_DWN_MIN.d: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.

TA_PTCH_FWD_MIN.d: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.

TA_PTCH_GSP_MIN.d: Minimum Groundspeed (not airspeed) to be flying for Pitching to be used.

TA_PTCH_TIMEOUT.d: Minimum down or forward distance must be triggered for more than this many seconds to start Pitching

TA_QUAD_DWN_MIN.d: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.

TA_QUAD_FWD_MIN.d: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.

TERR_BRK_ALT.d: terrain brake altitude. The altitude above the ground below which BRAKE mode will be engaged if in LOITER mode.

TERR_BRK_HDIST.d: terrain brake home distance. The distance from home where the auto BRAKE will be enabled. When within this distance of home the script will not activate

TERR_BRK_SPD.d: terrain brake speed threshold. Don't trigger BRAKE if both horizontal speed and descent rate are below this threshold. By setting this to a small value this can be used to allow the user to climb up to a safe altitude in LOITER mode. A value of 0.5 is recommended if you want to use LOITER to recover from an emergency terrain BRAKE mode change.

THR_KILL_CHAN.d: output channel to change on throttle kill, a value of zero disables the feature

THR_KILL_DEF.d: throttle kill default value. The default auxilliary function position on boot

THR_KILL_FUNC.d: AUX function to kill engine. This can be activated either with a RCn_OPTION and a R/C switch or with a ground station auxilliary function

THR_KILL_VAL.d: auxilliary value to kill throttle. Set to 2 to kill the throttle when the auxilliary is high. Set to 0 to kill when auxilliary is low

TOFSENSE_ID1.d: First TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. Leave this at 0 to accept all IDs and if only one sensor is present. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_ID2.d: Second TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. This cannot be 0. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_ID3.d: Third TOFSENSE-M sensor ID. This cannot be 0. You can change ID of sensor from NAssistant Software

TOFSENSE_INST1.d: First TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 1 will pick the first backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_INST2.d: Second TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 2 will pick the second backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_INST3.d: Third TOFSENSE-M sensors backend Instance. Setting this to 3 will pick the second backend from PRX_ or RNG_ Parameters (Depending on TOFSENSE_PRX)

TOFSENSE_MODE.d: TOFSENSE-M mode to be used. 0 for 8x8 mode. 1 for 4x4 mode. 0=8x8 mode, 1=4x4 mode.

TOFSENSE_NO.d: Number of TOFSENSE-M CAN sensors connected

TOFSENSE_PRX.d: Set 0 if sensor is to be used as a 1-D rangefinder (minimum of all distances will be sent, typically used for height detection). Set 1 if it should be used as a 3-D proximity device (Eg. Obstacle Avoidance). 0=Set as Rangefinder, 1=Set as Proximity sensor.

TOFSENSE_S1_BR.d: Serial Port baud rate. Sensor baud rate can be changed from Nassistant software

TOFSENSE_S1_PRX.d: Set 0 if sensor is to be used as a 1-D rangefinder (minimum of all distances will be sent, typically used for height detection). Set 1 if it should be used as a 3-D proximity device (Eg. Obstacle Avoidance). 0=Set as Rangefinder, 1=Set as Proximity sensor.

TOFSENSE_S1_SP.d: UART instance sensor is connected to. Set 1 if sensor is connected to the port with fist SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 28.

TRIK_ACT_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for trick action (abort,announce,execute)

TRIK_COUNT.d: Number of tricks which can be selected over the range of the trik selection RC channel

TRIK_ENABLE.d: Enables Tricks on Switch. TRIK params hidden until enabled

TRIK_SEL_FN.d: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for trick selection

VID1_CAMMODEL.d: Video stream camera model. 0=Unknown, 1=Siyi A8, 10=Herelink USB-tethering, 11=Topotek 1080p, 12=Topotek 480p, 13=Viewpro, 2=Siyi ZR10, 3=Siyi ZR30, 4=Siyi ZT30 Zoom, 5=Siyi ZT30 Wide, 6=Siyi ZT30 IR, 7=Siyi ZT6 RGB.

VID1_IPADDR0.d: Video stream IP Address first octet

VID1_IPADDR1.d: Video stream IP Address second octet

VID1_IPADDR2.d: Video stream IP Address third octet

VID1_IPADDR3.d: Video stream IP Address fourth octet

WEB_BLOCK_SIZE.d: web server block size for download

WEB_SENDFILE_MIN.d: sendfile is an offloading mechanism for faster file download. If this is non-zero and the file is larger than this size then sendfile will be used for file download

WINCH_RC_FUNC.d: RCn_OPTION number to use to control winch rate. 300=Scripting1, 301=Scripting2, 302=Scripting3, 303=Scripting4, 304=Scripting5, 305=Scripting6, 306=Scripting7, 307=Scripting8.

AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS.d: This sets margin for error in GPS derived altitude limit. This error margin is only used if the barometer has failed. If the barometer fails then the GPS will be used to enforce the AMSL_LIMIT, but this margin will be subtracted from the AMSL_LIMIT first, to ensure that even with the given amount of GPS altitude error the pressure altitude is not breached. OBC users should set this to comply with their D2 safety case. A value of -1 will mean that barometer failure will lead to immediate termination.

AFS_AMSL_LIMIT.d: This sets the AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude limit. If the pressure altitude determined by QNH exceeds this limit then flight termination will be forced. Note that this limit is in meters, whereas pressure altitude limits are often quoted in feet. A value of zero disables the pressure altitude limit.

AFS_DUAL_LOSS.d: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.

AFS_ENABLE.d: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect

AFS_GCS_TIMEOUT.d: The time (in seconds) of persistent data link loss before GCS failsafe occurs.

AFS_GEOFENCE.d: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

AFS_HB_PIN.d: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot. -1=Disabled, 113=BB Blue GP0 pin 6, 116=BB Blue GP0 pin 5, 49=BB Blue GP0 pin 4, 50=AUXOUT1, 51=AUXOUT2, 52=AUXOUT3, 53=AUXOUT4, 54=AUXOUT5, 55=AUXOUT6, 57=BB Blue GP0 pin 3.

AFS_MAN_PIN.d: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode. See the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS.d: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.

AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS.d: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.

AFS_MAX_RANGE.d: This is the maximum range of the vehicle in kilometers from first arming. If the vehicle goes beyond this range then the TERM_ACTION is performed. A value of zero disables this feature.

AFS_OPTIONS.d: See description for each bitmask bit description

AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.d: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.

AFS_RC.d: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME.d: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.

AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY.d: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.

AFS_TERMINATE.d: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal

AFS_TERM_ACTION.d: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup ArduPilot to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter

AFS_TERM_PIN.d: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot. -1=Disabled, 113=BB Blue GP0 pin 6, 116=BB Blue GP0 pin 5, 49=BB Blue GP0 pin 4, 50=AUXOUT1, 51=AUXOUT2, 52=AUXOUT3, 53=AUXOUT4, 54=AUXOUT5, 55=AUXOUT6, 57=BB Blue GP0 pin 3.

AFS_WP_COMMS.d: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss

AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS.d: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss

AHRS_COMP_BETA.d: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.d: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation. 0=Disabled, 10=Sim, 11=ExternalAHRS, 2=Enable EKF2, 3=Enable EKF3.

AHRS_GPS_GAIN.d: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

AHRS_GPS_MINSATS.d: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

AHRS_GPS_USE.d: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS according to its own parameters. A value of 2 means to use GPS for height as well as position - both in DCM estimation and when determining altitude-above-home. 0=Disabled, 1=Use GPS for DCM position, 2=Use GPS for DCM position and height.

AHRS_OPTIONS.d: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DontDisableAirspeedUsingEKF disables the EKF based innovation check for airspeed consistency. Setting AutoRecordOrigin will auto-save the EKF origin to parameters when it becomes valid.

AHRS_ORIENTATION.d: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for AHRS orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_ROT1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_ROT2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles. 0=None, 1=Yaw45, 10=Yaw90Roll180, 100=Custom 4.1 and older, 101=Custom 1, 102=Custom 2, 11=Yaw135Roll180, 12=Pitch180, 13=Yaw225Roll180, 14=Yaw270Roll180, 15=Yaw315Roll180, 16=Roll90.

AHRS_ORIGIN_ALT.d: AHRS last origin altitude in meters

AHRS_ORIGIN_LAT.d: AHRS last origin latitude in degrees

AHRS_ORIGIN_LON.d: AHRS last origin longitude in degrees

AHRS_RP_P.d: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

AHRS_TRIM_X.d: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

AHRS_TRIM_Y.d: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

AHRS_WIND_MAX.d: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor by clipping it to groundspeed plus/minus this limit. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_WIND_MAX to disable airspeed sensors.

AHRS_YAW_P.d: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

AIS_LIST_MAX.d: AIS list size of nearest vessels. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.

AIS_TIME_OUT.d: if no updates are received in this time a vessel will be removed from the list

ARMING_ACCTHRESH.d: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

ARMING_CRSDP_IGN.d: Must have value "1" if crashdump data is present on the system, or a prearm failure will be raised. Do not set this parameter unless the risks of doing so are fully understood. The presence of a crash dump means that the firmware currently installed has suffered a critical software failure which resulted in the autopilot immediately rebooting. The crashdump file gives diagnostic information which can help in finding the issue, please contact the ArduPIlot support team. If this crashdump data is present, the vehicle is likely unsafe to fly. Check the ArduPilot documentation for more details. 0=Crash Dump arming check active, 1=Crash Dump arming check deactivated.

ARMING_MAGTHRESH.d: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model. X and y axis are compared using this threhold, Z axis uses 2x this threshold. 0 to disable check

ARMING_MIS_ITEMS.d: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft

ARMING_NEED_LOC.d: Require that the vehicle have an absolute position before it arms. This can help ensure that the vehicle can Return To Launch. 0=Do not require location, 1=Require Location.

ARMING_OPTIONS.d: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour

ARMING_REQUIRE.d: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, all checks not skipped by ARMING_SKIPCHK must pass before the vehicle can be armed (for example, via rudder stick or GCS command). If 3, Arm immediately once pre-arm/arm checks are satisfied, but only one time per boot up. Note that a reboot is NOT required when setting to 0 but IS require when setting to 3. 0=No, 1=Yes(minimum PWM when disarmed), 3=No(AutoArmOnce after checks are passed).

ARMING_RUDDER.d: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ). Depending on vehicle type, arming in certain modes is prevented. See the wiki for each vehicle. Caution is recommended when arming if it is allowed in an auto-throttle mode!. 0=Disabled, 1=ArmingOnly, 2=ArmOrDisarm.

ARMING_SKIPCHK.d: Checks to skip prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks before allowing arming that will be skipped. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 0 (no checks skipped). In extreme circumstances, a value of -1 can be used to skip all non-mandatory current and future checks.

ARSPD_OPTIONS.d: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

ARSPD_PRIMARY.d: This selects which airspeed sensor will be the primary if multiple sensors are found. 0=FirstSensor, 1=2nd Sensor, 2=3rd Sensor, 3=4th Sensor, 4=5th Sensor, 5=6th Sensor.

ARSPD_TUBE_ORDER.d: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed. 0=Normal, 1=Swapped, 2=Auto Detect.

ARSPD_WIND_GATE.d: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle.

ARSPD_WIND_MAX.d: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

ARSPD_WIND_WARN.d: This parameter and function is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0.

ARSPD2_AUTOCAL.d: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

ARSPD2_BUS.d: Bus number of the I2C bus where the airspeed sensor is connected. May not correspond to board's I2C bus number labels. Retry another bus and reboot if airspeed sensor fails to initialize. 0=Bus0, 1=Bus1, 2=Bus2, 3=Bus3.

ARSPD2_DEVID.d: Airspeed sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

ARSPD2_PIN.d: The pin number that the airspeed sensor is connected to for analog sensors. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins". -1=Disabled, 100=PX4-v1, 13=Pixhawk2_PM2/CubeOrange_PM2, 14=CubeOrange, 16=Durandal, 2=Pixhawk/Pixracer/Navio2/Pixhawk2_PM1, 5=Navigator.

ARSPD2_PSI_RANGE.d: This parameter allows you to set the PSI (pounds per square inch) range for your sensor. You should not change this unless you examine the datasheet for your device

ARSPD2_RATIO.d: Calibrates pitot tube pressure to velocity. Increasing this value will indicate a higher airspeed at any given dynamic pressure.

ARSPD2_SKIP_CAL.d: This parameter allows you to skip airspeed offset calibration on startup, instead using the offset from the last calibration or requiring a manual calibration. This may be desirable if the offset variance between flights for your sensor is low and you want to avoid having to cover the pitot tube on each boot. 0=Disable, 1=Do not require offset calibration before flight. Manual calibration should be performed during initial setup., 2=Do not calibrate on start up. Manual calibration must be performed once per boot..

ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.d: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed. 0=Normal, 1=Swapped, 2=Auto Detect.

ARSPD2_TYPE.d: Type of airspeed sensor. 0=None, 1=I2C-MS4525D0, 10=I2C-DLVR-20in, 100=SITL, 11=I2C-DLVR-30in, 12=I2C-DLVR-60in, 13=NMEA water speed, 14=MSP, 15=ASP5033, 16=ExternalAHRS, 17=AUAV-10in, 18=AUAV-5in.

ARSPD2_USE.d: This parameter is not used by this vehicle. Always set to 0. 0=DoNotUse, 1=Use, 2=UseWhenZeroThrottle.

ARSPD3_AUTOCAL.d: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

ARSPD6_AUTOCAL.d: Enables automatic adjustment of airspeed ratio during a calibration flight based on estimation of ground speed and true airspeed. New ratio saved every 2 minutes if change is > 5%. Should not be left enabled.

ARSPD6_BUS.d: Bus number of the I2C bus where the airspeed sensor is connected. May not correspond to board's I2C bus number labels. Retry another bus and reboot if airspeed sensor fails to initialize. 0=Bus0, 1=Bus1, 2=Bus2, 3=Bus3.

ARSPD6_DEVID.d: Airspeed sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

ARSPD6_PIN.d: The pin number that the airspeed sensor is connected to for analog sensors. Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins". -1=Disabled, 100=PX4-v1, 13=Pixhawk2_PM2/CubeOrange_PM2, 14=CubeOrange, 16=Durandal, 2=Pixhawk/Pixracer/Navio2/Pixhawk2_PM1, 5=Navigator.

ARSPD6_PSI_RANGE.d: This parameter allows you to set the PSI (pounds per square inch) range for your sensor. You should not change this unless you examine the datasheet for your device

ARSPD6_RATIO.d: Calibrates pitot tube pressure to velocity. Increasing this value will indicate a higher airspeed at any given dynamic pressure.

ARSPD6_SKIP_CAL.d: This parameter allows you to skip airspeed offset calibration on startup, instead using the offset from the last calibration or requiring a manual calibration. This may be desirable if the offset variance between flights for your sensor is low and you want to avoid having to cover the pitot tube on each boot. 0=Disable, 1=Do not require offset calibration before flight. Manual calibration should be performed during initial setup., 2=Do not calibrate on start up. Manual calibration must be performed once per boot..

ARSPD6_TUBE_ORDR.d: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed. 0=Normal, 1=Swapped, 2=Auto Detect.

ATC_ACCEL_MAX.d: Speed control acceleration (and deceleration) maximum in m/s/s. 0 to disable acceleration limiting

ATC_BAL_D.d: Pitch control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch vs actual

ATC_BAL_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

ATC_BAL_FLTD.d: Pitch control Derivative filter frequency in Hz

ATC_BAL_FLTE.d: Pitch control Error filter frequency in Hz

ATC_BAL_FLTT.d: Pitch control Target filter frequency in Hz

ATC_BAL_I.d: Pitch control I gain for BalanceBots. Corrects long term error between the desired pitch (in radians) and actual pitch

ATC_BAL_IMAX.d: Pitch control I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate

ATC_BAL_LIM_TC.d: Pitch control limit time constant to protect against falling. Lower values limit pitch more quickly, higher values limit more slowly. Set to 0 to disable

ATC_BAL_LIM_THR.d: Pitch control limit throttle threshold. Pitch angle will be limited if throttle crosses this threshold (from 0 to 1)

ATC_BAL_NEF.d: Pitch control Error notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_BAL_NTF.d: Pitch control Target notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_BAL_P.d: Pitch control P gain for BalanceBots. Converts the error between the desired pitch (in radians) and actual pitch to a motor output (in the range -1 to +1)

ATC_BAL_PDMX.d: Pitch control PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

ATC_BAL_PIT_FF.d: Pitch control feed forward from current pitch angle

ATC_BAL_SMAX.d: Pitch control upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

ATC_BRAKE.d: Speed control brake enable/disable. Allows sending a reversed output to the motors to slow the vehicle. 0=Disable, 1=Enable.

ATC_DECEL_MAX.d: Speed control and deceleration maximum in m/s/s. 0 to use ATC_ACCEL_MAX for deceleration

ATC_SAIL_D.d: Sail Heel control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired heel angle vs actual

ATC_SAIL_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

ATC_SAIL_I.d: Sail Heel control I gain for sailboats. Corrects long term error between the desired heel angle (in radians) and actual

ATC_SAIL_IMAX.d: Sail Heel control I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum I term contribution to the main sail output (range -1 to +1)

ATC_SAIL_NEF.d: Sail Heel Error notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_SAIL_NTF.d: Sail Heel Target notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_SAIL_P.d: Sail Heel control P gain for sailboats. Converts the error between the desired heel angle (in radians) and actual heel to a main sail output (in the range -1 to +1)

ATC_SAIL_PDMX.d: Sail Heel control PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

ATC_SAIL_SMAX.d: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

ATC_SPEED_D.d: Speed control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired speed vs actual

ATC_SPEED_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

ATC_SPEED_I.d: Speed control I gain. Corrects long term error between the desired speed (in m/s) and actual speed

ATC_SPEED_IMAX.d: Speed control I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate

ATC_SPEED_NEF.d: Speed control Error notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_SPEED_NTF.d: Speed control Target notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_SPEED_P.d: Speed control P gain. Converts the error between the desired speed (in m/s) and actual speed to a motor output (in the range -1 to +1)

ATC_SPEED_PDMX.d: Speed control PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

ATC_SPEED_SMAX.d: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

ATC_STOP_SPEED.d: Speed control stop speed. Motor outputs to zero once vehicle speed falls below this value

ATC_STR_ACC_MAX.d: Steering control angular acceleration maximum (in deg/s/s). 0 to disable acceleration limiting

ATC_STR_ANG_P.d: Steering control angle P gain. Converts the error between the desired heading/yaw (in radians) and actual heading/yaw to a desired turn rate (in rad/sec)

ATC_STR_DEC_MAX.d: Steering control angular deceleration maximum (in deg/s/s). 0 to disable deceleration limiting

ATC_STR_RAT_D.d: Steering control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired turn rate vs actual

ATC_STR_RAT_D_FF.d: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target

ATC_STR_RAT_I.d: Steering control I gain. Corrects long term error between the desired turn rate (in rad/s) and actual

ATC_STR_RAT_IMAX.d: Steering control I gain maximum. Constrains the steering output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate

ATC_STR_RAT_MAX.d: Steering control rotation rate maximum in deg/s. 0 to remove rate limiting

ATC_STR_RAT_NEF.d: Steering control Error notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_STR_RAT_NTF.d: Steering control Target notch filter index, zero disables

ATC_STR_RAT_P.d: Steering control rate P gain. Converts the turn rate error (in radians/sec) to a steering control output (in the range -1 to +1)

ATC_STR_RAT_PDMX.d: Steering control PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output

ATC_STR_RAT_SMAX.d: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

ATC_TURN_MAX_G.d: The maximum turning acceleration (in units of gravities) that the rover can handle while remaining stable. The navigation code will keep the lateral acceleration below this level to avoid rolling over or slipping the wheels in turns

AVOID_ACCEL_MAX.d: Maximum acceleration with which obstacles will be avoided with. Set zero to disable acceleration limits

AVOID_BACKUP_DZ.d: Distance beyond AVOID_MARGIN parameter, after which vehicle will backaway from obstacles. Increase this parameter if you see vehicle going back and forth in front of obstacle.

AVOID_BACKUP_SPD.d: Maximum speed that will be used to back away from obstacles horizontally in position control modes (m/s). Set zero to disable horizontal backup.

AVOID_BACKZ_SPD.d: Maximum speed that will be used to back away from obstacles vertically in height control modes (m/s). Set zero to disable vertical backup.

AVOID_MARGIN.d: Vehicle will attempt to stay at least this distance (in meters) from objects while in GPS modes

BARO1_DEVID.d: Barometer sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

BARO1_THST_SCALE.d: Thrust scaling in Pascals. This value scaled by the normalized thrust is subtracted from the barometer pressure. This is used to adjust linearly based on the thrust output for local pressure difference induced by the props.

BARO2_DEVID.d: Barometer2 sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

BARO3_DEVID.d: Barometer3 sensor ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

BARO_ALT_OFFSET.d: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

BARO_EXT_BUS.d: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the BARO_PROBE_EXT parameter. -1=Disabled, 0=Bus0, 1=Bus1, 6=Bus6.

BARO_FIELD_ELV.d: User provided field elevation in meters. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. Changes to this parameter will only be used when disarmed. A value of 0 means the EKF origin height is used for takeoff height above sea level.

BARO_FLTR_RNG.d: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

BARO_GND_TEMP.d: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

BARO_PRIMARY.d: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found. 0=FirstBaro, 1=2ndBaro, 2=3rdBaro.

BARO_PROBE_EXT.d: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on BARO_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in BARO_EXT_BUS.

BARO_THST_FILT.d: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency for thrust compensation. This smooths the throttle input to prevent rapid baro altitude changes during throttle transients. Set to 0 to disable filtering.

BARO1_WCF_BCK.d: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the X body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during backwards flight, then this will be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

BARO1_WCF_DN.d: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the Z body axis. If the baro height estimate rises above truth height during descending flight (or forward flight with a high backwards lean angle, eg braking manoeuvre), then this should be a negative number. Multirotors can use this feature only if using EKF3 and if the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters have been tuned.

BARO1_WCF_ENABLE.d: This enables the use of wind coefficients for barometer compensation. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

BARO1_WCF_FWD.d: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a positive wind relative velocity along the X body axis. BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

BATT2_AMP_PERVLT.d: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to.

BATT2_ARM_MAH.d: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATT2_ARM_VOLT parameter.

BATT2_ARM_VOLT.d: Battery voltage level which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any voltage.

BATT2_CAPACITY.d: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

BATT2_CFG_UPDATE.d: Controls startup configuration behavior. 1 writes configuration once then clears to 0. 2 checks current configuration and writes only if needed. 0=Disabled, 1=Write configuration once, 2=Check and update if needed.

BATT2_CHANNEL.d: INA3221 channel to return data for

BATT2_CRT_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATT2_CRT_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATT2_CURR_MULT.d: Multiplier applied to all current related reports to allow for adjustment if no UAVCAN param access or current splitting applications

BATT2_CURR_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for Current monitoring on AD7091R5. -1=Disabled.

BATT2_ESC_INDEX.d: ESC Telemetry Index to write voltage, current, consumption and temperature data to. Use 0 to disable.

BATT2_ESC_MASK.d: If 0 all connected ESCs will be used. If non-zero, only those selected in the bitmask will be used.

BATT2_FL_FLTR.d: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. A value of -1 disables the filter and unfiltered voltage is used to determine the fuel level. The suggested values at in the range of 0.2 Hz to 0.5 Hz.

BATT2_FL_PIN.d: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to.Analog Airspeed or RSSI ports can be used for Analog input( some autopilots provide others also). Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins". -1=Disabled, 100=PX4-v1, 13=Pixhawk2_PM2/CubeOrange_PM2, 14=CubeOrange, 16=Durandal, 2=Pixhawk/Pixracer/Navio2/Pixhawk2_PM1, 5=Navigator.

BATT2_FL_VLT_MIN.d: The voltage seen on the analog pin when the fuel tank is empty. Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATT2_FL_V_MULT.d: Voltage multiplier to determine what the full tank voltage reading is. This is calculated as 1 / (Voltage_Full - Voltage_Empty) Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATT2_FS_VOLTSRC.d: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event. 0=Raw Voltage, 1=Sag Compensated Voltage.

BATT2_I2C_ADDR.d: Battery monitor I2C address. If this is zero then probe list of supported addresses

BATT2_LOW_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATT2_MAX_AMPS.d: This controls the maximum current the INA239 sensor will work with.

BATT2_MAX_VOLT.d: Maximum voltage of battery. Provides scaling of current versus voltage

BATT2_MONITOR.d: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current. 0=Disabled, 10=Sum Of Selected Monitors, 11=FuelFlow, 12=FuelLevelPWM, 13=SMBUS-SUI3, 14=SMBUS-SUI6, 15=NeoDesign, 16=SMBus-Maxell, 17=Generator-Elec, 18=Generator-Fuel, 19=Rotoye, 20=MPPT.

BATT2_OPTIONS.d: This sets options to change the behaviour of the battery monitor

BATT2_SERIAL_NUM.d: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With DroneCan it is the battery_id.

BATTB_ESC_MASK.d: If 0 all connected ESCs will be used. If non-zero, only those selected in the bitmask will be used.

BATTB_FL_FLTR.d: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. A value of -1 disables the filter and unfiltered voltage is used to determine the fuel level. The suggested values at in the range of 0.2 Hz to 0.5 Hz.

BATTB_FL_PIN.d: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to.Analog Airspeed or RSSI ports can be used for Analog input( some autopilots provide others also). Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins". -1=Disabled, 100=PX4-v1, 13=Pixhawk2_PM2/CubeOrange_PM2, 14=CubeOrange, 16=Durandal, 2=Pixhawk/Pixracer/Navio2/Pixhawk2_PM1, 5=Navigator.

BATTB_FL_VLT_MIN.d: The voltage seen on the analog pin when the fuel tank is empty. Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATTB_FL_V_MULT.d: Voltage multiplier to determine what the full tank voltage reading is. This is calculated as 1 / (Voltage_Full - Voltage_Empty) Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATTB_FS_CRT_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATTB_FS_LOW_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATTB_FS_VOLTSRC.d: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event. 0=Raw Voltage, 1=Sag Compensated Voltage.

BATTB_I2C_ADDR.d: Battery monitor I2C address. If this is zero then probe list of supported addresses

BATTB_LOW_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTB_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATTB_LOW_TIMER.d: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

BATTB_LOW_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATTB_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTB_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATTB_MAX_AMPS.d: This controls the maximum current the INA239 sensor will work with.

BATTB_MAX_VOLT.d: Maximum voltage of battery. Provides scaling of current versus voltage

BATTB_MONITOR.d: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current. 0=Disabled, 10=Sum Of Selected Monitors, 11=FuelFlow, 12=FuelLevelPWM, 13=SMBUS-SUI3, 14=SMBUS-SUI6, 15=NeoDesign, 16=SMBus-Maxell, 17=Generator-Elec, 18=Generator-Fuel, 19=Rotoye, 20=MPPT.

BATTB_OPTIONS.d: This sets options to change the behaviour of the battery monitor

BATTB_SERIAL_NUM.d: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With DroneCan it is the battery_id.

BATTB_SHUNT.d: This sets the shunt resistor used in the device

BATTB_SUM_MASK.d: 0: sum of remaining battery monitors, If none 0 sum of specified monitors. Current will be summed and voltages averaged.

BATTB_VOLT_MULT.d: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATTB_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT).

BATTB_VOLT_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for voltage monitoring on AD7091R5. -1=Disabled.

This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

BATTC_AMP_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

BATTC_AMP_PERVLT.d: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to.

BATTF_LOW_TIMER.d: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

BATTF_LOW_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATTF_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTF_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

BATTF_MAX_AMPS.d: This controls the maximum current the INA239 sensor will work with.

BATTF_MAX_VOLT.d: Maximum voltage of battery. Provides scaling of current versus voltage

BATTF_MONITOR.d: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current. 0=Disabled, 10=Sum Of Selected Monitors, 11=FuelFlow, 12=FuelLevelPWM, 13=SMBUS-SUI3, 14=SMBUS-SUI6, 15=NeoDesign, 16=SMBus-Maxell, 17=Generator-Elec, 18=Generator-Fuel, 19=Rotoye, 20=MPPT.

BATTF_OPTIONS.d: This sets options to change the behaviour of the battery monitor

BATTF_SERIAL_NUM.d: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With DroneCan it is the battery_id.

BATTF_SHUNT.d: This sets the shunt resistor used in the device

BATTF_SUM_MASK.d: 0: sum of remaining battery monitors, If none 0 sum of specified monitors. Current will be summed and voltages averaged.

BATTF_VLT_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset on voltage pin. This allows for an offset due to a diode. This voltage is subtracted before the scaling is applied

BATTF_VOLT_MULT.d: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATTF_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT).

BATTF_VOLT_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for voltage monitoring on AD7091R5. -1=Disabled.

BATTF_WATT_MAX.d: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

BATTG_AMP_OFFSET.d: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

BATTG_AMP_PERVLT.d: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to.

BATTG_ARM_MAH.d: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATTG_ARM_VOLT parameter.

BATTG_ARM_VOLT.d: Battery voltage level which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any voltage.

BATTG_CAPACITY.d: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

BATTG_CFG_UPDATE.d: Controls startup configuration behavior. 1 writes configuration once then clears to 0. 2 checks current configuration and writes only if needed. 0=Disabled, 1=Write configuration once, 2=Check and update if needed.

BATTG_CHANNEL.d: INA3221 channel to return data for

BATTG_CRT_MAH.d: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTG_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATTG_CRT_VOLT.d: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATTG_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATTG_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

BATTG_CURR_MULT.d: Multiplier applied to all current related reports to allow for adjustment if no UAVCAN param access or current splitting applications

BATTG_CURR_PIN.d: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for Current monitoring on AD7091R5. -1=Disabled.

BATTG_ESC_INDEX.d: ESC Telemetry Index to write voltage, current, consumption and temperature data to. Use 0 to disable.

BATTG_ESC_MASK.d: If 0 all connected ESCs will be used. If non-zero, only those selected in the bitmask will be used.

BATTG_FL_FLTR.d: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. A value of -1 disables the filter and unfiltered voltage is used to determine the fuel level. The suggested values at in the range of 0.2 Hz to 0.5 Hz.

BATTG_FL_PIN.d: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to.Analog Airspeed or RSSI ports can be used for Analog input( some autopilots provide others also). Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins". -1=Disabled, 100=PX4-v1, 13=Pixhawk2_PM2/CubeOrange_PM2, 14=CubeOrange, 16=Durandal, 2=Pixhawk/Pixracer/Navio2/Pixhawk2_PM1, 5=Navigator.

BATTG_FL_VLT_MIN.d: The voltage seen on the analog pin when the fuel tank is empty. Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATTG_FL_V_MULT.d: Voltage multiplier to determine what the full tank voltage reading is. This is calculated as 1 / (Voltage_Full - Voltage_Empty) Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.

BATTG_FS_CRT_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATTG_FS_LOW_ACT.d: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe. 0=Warn only, 1=RTL, 2=Hold, 3=SmartRTL, 4=SmartRTL or Hold, 5=Terminate, 6=Loiter or Hold.

BATTG_FS_VOLTSRC.d: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event. 0=Raw Voltage, 1=Sag Compensated Voltage.

BATTG_I2C_ADDR.d: Battery monitor I2C address. If this is zero then probe list of supported addresses

BCN_ALT.d: Beacon origin's altitude above sealevel in meters

BCN_ORIENT_YAW.d: Beacon systems rotation from north in degrees

BCN_TYPE.d: What type of beacon based position estimation device is connected. 0=None, 1=Pozyx, 10=SITL, 2=Marvelmind, 3=Nooploop.

BRD_ALT_CONFIG.d: Select an alternative hardware configuration. A value of zero selects the default configuration for this board. Other values are board specific. Please see the documentation for your board for details on any alternative configuration values that may be available.

BRD_BOOT_DELAY.d: This adds a delay in milliseconds to boot to ensure peripherals initialise fully

BRD_HEAT_LOWMGN.d: Arming check will fail if temp is lower than this margin below BRD_HEAT_TARG. 0 disables the low temperature check

BRD_HEAT_TARG.d: Board heater target temperature for boards with controllable heating units. Set to -1 to disable the heater, please reboot after setting to -1.

BRD_IDLE_STATS.d: Capture and calculate true CPU load using idle threads. 0=Disable, 1=Enable.

BRD_IO_DSHOT.d: This loads the DShot firmware on the IO co-processor. 0=StandardFW, 1=DshotFW.

BRD_IO_ENABLE.d: This allows for the IO co-processor on boards with an IOMCU to be disabled. Setting to 2 will enable the IOMCU but not attempt to update firmware on startup. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=EnableNoFWUpdate.

BRD_PWM_VOLT_SEL.d: This sets the voltage max for PWM output pulses. 0 for 3.3V and 1 for 5V output. On boards with an IOMCU that support this parameter this option only affects the 8 main outputs, not the 6 auxiliary outputs. Using 5V output can help to reduce the impact of ESC noise interference corrupting signals to the ESCs. 0=3.3V, 1=5V.

BRD_SAFETYOPTION.d: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed

BRD_SAFETY_DEFLT.d: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled.

BRD_SAFETY_MASK.d: A bitmask which controls what outputs can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

BRD_SBUS_OUT.d: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz. 0=Disabled, 1=50Hz, 2=75Hz, 3=100Hz, 4=150Hz, 5=200Hz, 6=250Hz, 7=300Hz.

BRD_SD_FENCE.d: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in fence.stg for fence storage.

BRD_SD_MISSION.d: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in mission.stg for waypoint storage. Each waypoint uses 15 bytes.

BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN.d: This is a scaling factor to slow down microSD operation. It can be used on flight board and microSD card combinations where full speed is not reliable. For normal full speed operation a value of 0 should be used.

BRD_SER1_RTSCTS.d: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1). You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Auto, 3=RS-485 Driver enable RTS pin.

BRD_SER2_RTSCTS.d: Enable flow control on serial 2 (telemetry 2). You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Auto, 3=RS-485 Driver enable RTS pin.

BRD_SER3_RTSCTS.d: Enable flow control on serial 3. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. 0=Disabled, 1=Enabled, 2=Auto, 3=RS-485 Driver enable RTS pin.
